key_concepts: Soluble solutes dissolve easily in a solvent due to similar nature.
Insoluble solutes do not dissolve because of differences in nature.
Sugar and salt dissolve in water; butter is insoluble in water.
Miscible liquids mix completely; immiscible liquids separate.
Alcohol and water are miscible; water and oil are immiscible.
Dissolving mixes solute particles into a solvent without losing them.
Melting is a solid changing to liquid due to heat.
Temperature affects dissolving and melting by changing particle kinetic energy.
Concentration measures the relative amount of solute and solvent.
Concentrated solutions have relatively large amount of solute; diluted have small amount.
Percent by mass = (mass of solute / mass of solution) × 100.
A 5% bleach solution contains 5 g sodium hypochlorite per 100 g bleach.
